chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus from Umar ibn Abi Hafsh, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Fear Allah and upon you is [the obligation of] fulfilling the trust to whoever entrusted you with it. So even if the killer of Ali (peace be upon him) entrusted me with fulfilling a trust, I would fulfill it for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of fulfilling trusts to enemies in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the concept of *amanah* (trustworthiness) to a universal duty, independent of the recipient's merit or relationship to the giver. By citing the killer of Imam Ali as a hypothetical example, he demonstrates that fidelity to one's word is an intrinsic virtue rather than a reciprocal social contract, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding commercial and personal trusts. This underscores the sincerity (*ikhlas*) required in fulfilling obligations, even towards those who may be unjust to us.
